transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-04
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~57 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Ortiz (Redwood SE), Lena Morales (Peregrine - Head of MLOps), Tom Reed (Peregrine - CTO), Priya Singh (Peregrine SRE)

Summary:
- Quarterly operational check focusing on runway, costs, and upcoming pilot handoff.
- Discussed dedicated vs private deployment tradeoffs, cost levers (batching, quantization), and reliability needs (SLOs/SLA).
- Agreed to run a performance benchmark and exchange security artifacts; clear next steps and owners recorded.

Topics covered:
1) Usage pattern & cost breakdown
2) Reliability / incident history and SLA targets
3) Pilot scope: dataset, endpoints, and metrics
4) Deployment options: Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC
5) Security/compliance: KMS, audit logs, SSO/SAML

Transcript body:
[00:00] Samir: Hey, everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick kickoff — this is Samir from Redwood, i'll run through the agenda.
[00:10] Lena: yeah hi, thanks. we only have an hour. recent Q2 usage jumped and we want to make sure the pilot and the runway align.
[00:18] Tom: morning all, high-level we need predictability — our finance team flagged the token cost variance last month.
[00:24] Maya: understood. i'll start with the telemetry we saw — current token mix is 65% short chat, 25% long-context rerank, 10% embeddings, roughly. that split is driving most of the token burn.
[00:36] Priya: and we saw two incidents in July that spiked latency; hoping to understand mitigation.
[00:40] Maya: right, the July spike aligned with a model rollout and an autoscaler misconfig — where requests queued and batching behavior escalated latency. we have a couple of guardrails we can enable.
[00:50] Lena: can you remind us of the batching tradeoffs? we need low 95th p99 for user-facing flows.
[00:56] Maya: yes, there are steady-state batching gains — batching reduces per-token cost but increases tail latency depending on arrival pattern. Redwood Dedicated can give you reserved throughput and lower tail because you avoid noisy neighbors; Private VPC gives the same control but with your network boundaries.
[01:12] Tom: what's realistic p95/p99 for a dedicated pool?
[01:15] Maya: for a 1k concurrency pool on A100s, we've observed p95 around 150-200 ms for short chats and p99 under 400 ms with continuous batching tuned. but that's model and prompt dependent — you'll see variance with long-context rerank jobs.
[01:30] Samir: we should caveat the numbers — they come from our catalog but your prompts will change it — hence the benchmark.
[01:36] Priya: okay. security: we need KMS/HSM integration, audit logs exported to our SIEM, and SSO via SAML. does Redwood support Gov-like key isolation?
[01:46] Samir: yes, we support customer-managed keys (KMS) in Private deployments and Dedicated customers can request HSM-backed key management. we'll send the integration notes; also audit logs are available for retention and forwarding.
[01:56] Lena: perfect. on retention, do you allow configurable retention windows per route?
[02:02] Maya: yes — you can set retention at route level and define redaction rules. we'll share the config doc.
[02:08] Tom: costs again — any quick levers we can take before the pilot? quantization? model swap?
[02:14] Maya: quantized model variants often give 2-4x throughput improvements for heavy embedding/transform workloads with modest quality tradeoffs. swapping to a slightly smaller LLM or using a rererank pipeline that uses a cached candidate set also helps. then batching and prefix caching will give you immediate wins.
[02:30] Lena: caching — we have a lot of repeated prefixes in our chat flows. how much can that reduce tokens?
[02:34] Maya: depends, but we've seen prefix/KV cache cut token generation by 20-40% for product-help style prompts. for high repeat queries, it's higher.
[02:44] Priya: for the incidents, what's Redwood's typical on-call cadence and support SLA on Dedicated?
[02:49] Samir: Dedicated customers get NBD support with escalation paths; for enterprise we have 24x7 with SLO-backed response times. we'll include the SLA doc.
[02:58] Tom: good. pilot scope — we want to run two endpoints: 1) user chat for support triage (low latency), 2) nightly rerank job for recommendations (throughput). success criteria: p95 < 250ms for chat, rerank throughput >= 2000 docs/min with median latency < 2s, and cost per 1k sessions below $X (finance to accept).
[03:22] Lena: [overlap] and we want model stability — rollback mechanisms must be simple.
[03:26] Maya: rollouts: Redwood supports canary ramping, A/B, and automatic fallback to smaller variants if error rates climb. se will help script the rollout.
[03:36] Priya: network egress — if we do Private VPC, can we keep traffic on-prem for PII?
[03:41] Samir: yes, Private deployment keeps data in your VPC; optionally, we can do an on-prem package if you need air-gapped processing.
[03:48] Tom: what's the timeline to spin up a dedicated pool + run the benchmark?
[03:52] Maya: spinning a small dedicated pool is typically 2-3 business days after contract and onboarding; benchmark scheduling depends on you sending anonymized traces. i'd plan 2 weeks for full run and analysis.
[04:02] Lena: okay, so action items from us: provide sample traces and confirm SLA numbers.
[04:06] Samir: and from Redwood: cost model, security docs, benchmark runbook. we'll deliver those by the dates we discussed.
[04:12] Tom: one more question — competitor comparisons. we ran a quick bake against the cloud vendor and saw better tail latency with Redwood in our last test but cost calculations were rough. can you give a side-by-side that includes caching and batching effects?
[04:26] Samir: yes, we'll include a comparative sheet. note that vendor numbers often assume different concurrency and no persistent KV cache, so we'll normalize for your workload.
[04:36] Priya: on observability, we need token-level breakdowns and per-route tracing. how granular is the cost telemetry?
[04:42] Maya: token-level billing, route-level, and per-model breakouts are in Console — and you can attach traces to each request id. we'll show a live dashboard in the benchmark.
[04:50] Lena: great. any blockers to pilot signoff from Redwood side?
[04:54] Samir: contract-level: nothing unusual. we do need the scope and commitment window so we can size capacity and reserve.
[05:01] Tom: procurement also needs an estimate for committed vs pay-as-you-go to compare. can you provide both?
[05:06] Samir: yes. we'll model a monthly committed pool vs hosted overages in the cost model.
[05:12] Maya: quick note — for the rerank pipeline, we can propose a hybrid routing policy so rerank jobs run on lower-cost nodes during off-peak and fallback to dedicated during day. that preserves budget and SLA.
[05:24] Priya: sounds good.
[05:26] Samir: ok, wrapping — recap of next steps and owners, and we'll schedule the benchmark for week of Sep 20 pending trace delivery.
[05:33] Lena: thanks everyone.
[05:36] Tom: thanks.

End of transcript.
